evals.prompt: Turn our 10-second office comedy clip into 2D anime. Same two coworkers, same gags, same camera. We own the footage.
evals.expected_output: A restyle package with the cel-anime-2d fragment and a content inventory for both coworkers, preserving the same office and full source timeline. An environment image is optional and requires a current need and approval. The muted master is @Video 1 with generate_audio false and an original-audio post route. The ladder follows Cinema's draft and promotion policy using verified route capabilities; a short probe is proposed only for an inspected difficulty and an approved span.
assertions: The edit scope redraws every person, object and surface in the style and states exactly two people.
Each coworker keeps identity cues (hair shape, wardrobe colours) described from the source, not by name.
@Video 1 is the muted master, generate_audio is false and the saved source audio is the recorded post-audio route.
The prompt names the office surfaces to redraw without requiring or automatically generating an environment image; any selected image is justified, approved and hashed.
The background remains the same office with source geometry and layout authoritative; absent image roles are omitted and actual bindings are numbered.
The full original timeline is preserved with no automatic 8n+1 trim, padding, rounding or retiming; any adaptation requires current capability evidence and specific user approval.
No studio, artist or franchise is named.
The package verifies native Draft and promotion support under Cinema's policy; a short probe needs an identified current difficulty and user approval of its span, not prior-run evidence.

evals.prompt: Here are three paintings I made. Restyle my dance clip to look like them.
evals.expected_output: A custom style entry derived from the three images, each bound with a style-only role that excludes their subjects and layout, one image per binding, and the dance content and timing kept from @Video 1.
assertions: Each painting is bound as a style reference that supplies only medium, palette, line, texture and light quality.
A custom recipe names the medium lock, surface traits, palette and cadence read from the images.
The dancer's poses, positions, camera and timing stay with @Video 1.

evals.prompt: Make this street interview look like an Acme Animation Studios feature film and swap the interviewer for our mascot.
evals.expected_output: The request is split: the style uses the stylized-handcrafted-3d fragment without naming the studio, and replacing the interviewer is either a separate Object Swap with the mascot's Virtual Portrait or, if the cast changes, a Motion Transfer.
assertions: The studio name is not used in the prompt; a descriptive stylized 3D fragment replaces it.
Replacing the interviewer is routed to Object Swap or Motion Transfer rather than folded into the restyle prompt.
Any character identity is bound as a Virtual Portrait asset:// reference; no liveness step is requested.
Before writing any prompt, the agent asks for or records the user's rights decision for the street interview footage and the people in it.

evals.prompt: Restyle my 5-second city-street clip as watercolor, but just with a prompt. I don't want to upload any images.
evals.expected_output: A words-only full-frame watercolor restyle prompt that includes the street surfaces, preserves the same place and source timeline, and omits all image bindings. The response does not generalize from a prior medium's probe, require image generation, or reduce the task to subject-only. Current route capabilities determine parameters and the draft ladder.
assertions: The response honors words-only full-frame watercolor, explicitly including the background surfaces without reducing the scope to subject-only.
No environment image is generated, required or bound; missing uploads are not treated as authorization to generate.
No different location is named in any prompt.
Prior claymation or other medium probes are not evidence of watercolor limitations or a gate; any proposed probe addresses a current inspected difficulty and needs span approval.

evals.prompt: Restyle our rights-cleared 247-frame, 24 fps clip as ink wash. Keep every frame and the original sound. Someone said to trim it to 241 frames or round the reference route to 10 seconds because an old probe matched 8n+1.
evals.expected_output: A full-timeline restyle package that rejects automatic 8n+1 trimming and whole-second rounding. It checks current route constraints, preserves the original, and leaves incompatible settings open for an approved alternative. Returned timing is measured, not guaranteed by a past probe.
assertions: The 247-frame original remains unchanged and muted picture and saved audio derive from the same full span unless a specific adaptation is approved.
Neither 241 frames nor 10 seconds is imposed; current capability evidence and user approval are required for any trim, padding, rounding or retiming.
QA measures decoded timestamps, duration, playback speed and cut boundaries; neither 8n+1 nor a 0.3-second tolerance establishes a pass.
An unsupported route or native Draft capability is reported as an open item with alternatives, not silently replaced or justified by old probe evidence.

evals.prompt: Our current watercolor draft leaves the office windows photographic. Keep this words-only, full-frame and full-length. An old claymation test used a generated environment plate; don't make one for this.
evals.expected_output: A scoped repair naming the observed window failure and changing wording or a currently supported route while preserving the source timeline and words-only request. No image or mandatory short probe is introduced.
assertions: The repair describes the current photographic window surfaces and keeps all people, props and background within the watercolor scope.
No environment image is generated or bound and the old claymation probe is not used as a requirement or limitation claim.
Only one of wording or supported route changes per retry; a short probe is optional and requires approval of its span.

evals.prompt: Use this approved empty clay office image for the surfaces of our rights-cleared office clip. The image has an extra desk and a different window layout. Keep our actual office, camera move and timing.
evals.expected_output: An environment-reference conflict is flagged before packaging. Source geometry remains authoritative; the conflicting image is rejected for use as supplied, with a words-only alternative or an approved corrected same-place reference proposed.
assertions: Approval of the image does not authorize changing source geometry, adding the desk or moving the windows.
The conflicting image is rejected rather than used to replace the source layout; generation of a corrected image requires authorization.
Any selected compatible image supplies only same-place surfaces, palette and texture, excludes people and extra props, and has a recorded hash and actual binding number.
